q: Who proposed the Garden City model?
n: Ebenezer Howard developed the Garden City idea as a planned settlement model intended to combine urban opportunities with access to nature. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Garden City.

q: What term is commonly used for an urban area with more than 10 million inhabitants?
n: A megacity is commonly defined as an urban agglomeration with a population of at least 10 million. UN DESA — World Urbanization Prospects.

q: Using the same site-planning convention, where is the preferred location for a septic tank on a 10% slope?
n: The source set places the septic tank toward the lower portion of the site so wastewater can generally flow by gravity. Actual siting depends on soil, setbacks, groundwater, and local sanitation rules. U.S. EPA — Septic Systems.

q: When a desirable park view lies across the road, which response best preserves that visual advantage?
o: Place the drop-off along the road
Add sun-shading devices to the windows
Add a porch at the main entry
Plant trees in front of the building
n: Window shading can control glare and solar gain while preserving the outward view; placing tall trees directly in front of the building would tend to obstruct it. Whole Building Design Guide — Daylighting.

q: Who prepared the major plans associated with the redevelopment of Manila and the new summer capital at Baguio?
n: Daniel Burnham prepared the major planning proposals for Manila and Baguio during the American colonial period. ArchDaily — Daniel Burnham’s Manila and Baguio plans.

q: What term describes the large-scale concentration of people into cities and the resulting growth of urban areas?
n: Urbanization is the process in which increasing numbers of people live in urban areas, contributing to the growth of cities. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Urbanization.

q: What term refers to surface features of Earth such as valleys, hills, mountains, and plateaus?
n: A landform is a natural physical feature of Earth’s surface, including hills, valleys, mountains, and plateaus. USGS — Geologic History.

q: In the same general zoning convention, what color identifies parks and recreation areas?
n: The cited Philippine zoning reference uses dark green for open space/urban parks, while other green shades may represent different land-use categories. Philippine Zoning Color Legend — Open Space/Urban Parks.

q: Who is associated with the regular Greek grid plan and the integrated agora, often called the first town planner?
n: Hippodamus of Miletus is strongly associated with the systematic grid plan and planning of civic spaces in Greek cities. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Hippodamus.

q: Which neighborhood-planning model is designed for roughly 5,000–9,000 residents, with a school and shared community facilities near the center?
n: The Neighborhood Unit organizes a residential population around a central school and other shared facilities, with local streets protecting the interior from through traffic. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Clarence Perry / Neighborhood Unit.

q: What term describes soil that readily allows gravity water to move downward without prolonged saturation?
n: Good drainage describes soil conditions in which excess water can move away instead of remaining saturated for long periods. Source: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service — Soil Drainage. USDA NRCS — Soil Drainage.

q: What is the upper boundary of the saturated zone in an unconfined aquifer?
n: The water table is the upper surface of the saturated zone in an unconfined groundwater system. U.S. Geological Survey — Aquifers and Groundwater.

q: Which ancient Mesopotamian city became especially famous for its monumental walls and major buildings?
n: Babylon was a major Mesopotamian capital renowned for monumental architecture, defensive works, and urban development. UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Babylon.

q: Who developed the master plan for Chandigarh, one of India’s earliest major planned cities after independence?
n: Le Corbusier developed the master plan for Chandigarh after an earlier planning scheme, shaping its sector-based urban structure and major civic core. UNESCO — Chandigarh.

q: Which is not an immediate planning consequence typically associated with rapid rural-to-urban migration?
n: Rapid urban growth can strain housing, infrastructure, and services, while road widening is a specific policy response rather than an automatic consequence of migration. UN-Habitat — Urbanization and Housing.

q: What is the main drainage concern commonly associated with nearly flat sites?
n: Flat terrain tends to have less natural relief for runoff, so poor drainage can increase ponding and surface-flooding risk. FEMA — Flooding and Flood Risk.

q: Which ancient settlement is identified with one of the world’s earliest permanent communities and an early defensive wall?
n: Ancient Jericho/Tell es-Sultan contains early permanent settlement remains and monumental fortification features dating to the Neolithic period. UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Ancient Jericho/Tell es-Sultan.

q: Which urban model explains city growth as a set of concentric zones expanding outward from a central core?
n: The concentric-zone model represents urban land uses as rings expanding outward from the center; Ernest Burgess is the theorist most closely associated with it. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Urban Ecology.

q: What term refers to low-density outward expansion of housing, commerce, and roads over large areas with limited coordinated planning?
n: Urban sprawl describes dispersed outward growth of developed land, often characterized by low density and extensive reliance on roads. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Urban Sprawl.

q: For the site-planning convention used in this reviewer, where is the preferred location for a water tank on a 10% sloping site?
n: The reviewer’s site-planning rule places the water tank at the highest practical point so elevation can assist distribution by gravity. This is a planning convention; actual tank placement must still follow project engineering and code requirements. Whole Building Design Guide — Water Systems.

q: For traffic safety, how should a primary driveway or drop-off be positioned relative to a major street intersection?
o: Set back with adequate corner clearance
n: Access points should be spaced away from intersections to reduce conflict points and protect intersection operations. The exact clearance is site- and roadway-specific. Federal Highway Administration — Corridor Access Management.

q: Which Spanish colonial planning law established a central plaza with important buildings and a regular street pattern for new towns?
n: The Laws of the Indies codified planning principles for Spanish colonial settlements, including the central plaza and ordered street layout. UNESCO — Colonial Urban Plan of Manila.

q: Which option is not one of Kevin Lynch’s five core elements used to describe a city’s image?
n: Lynch identified paths, edges, districts, nodes, and landmarks as the five key elements used to structure a mental image of a city. Kevin Lynch urban-image overview — ArchDaily.

q: What is the rate at which water moves through a soil or other porous material called?
n: Permeability describes how readily a fluid passes through a material; in soil and groundwater work, hydraulic conductivity is commonly used to quantify water movement. Source: U.S. EPA — Soil Water Movement. U.S. EPA — Soil Water Movement.

q: In the general Philippine zoning color convention used in the source set, which color represents industrial zones?
n: The general Philippine zoning color legend used in planning references assigns violet/purple to industrial zones. Philippine Local Government Zoning Ordinance — Land Use Color Coding.

q: What was the principal civic gathering place in an ancient Greek city-state?
n: The agora served as a public gathering and civic space and supported commercial, social, political, and cultural activity. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Agora.

q: Who won the competition for the master plan of Brasília?
n: Lúcio Costa won the competition for Brasília’s master plan; Oscar Niemeyer designed many of its major buildings. UNESCO — Brasília / Modern Brazilian Architecture.

q: Which field studies Earth’s composition, surface-forming processes, and geologic history?
n: Geology studies Earth materials, structure, processes, and history; the other choices focus on water, landform processes, or spatial description. USGS — The Interior of the Earth.

q: What structure is used to hold soil or rock where a slope is steeper than its natural angle of repose?
n: Retaining walls stabilize and restrain soil or rock masses where an unsupported slope would be unstable. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers — Retaining Walls.

q: Which is not usually grouped among the earliest primary river-valley civilizations?
n: Mesopotamia, Egypt, and the Indus Valley are conventionally identified as major early river-valley civilizations; ancient Greece developed later and under different geographic conditions. Encyclopaedia Britannica — Ancient Civilizations.
